mainTopic: Where the rule comes from that certain big trees are not sold with a field, and how a seller's exact wording decides which trees, palms and vines are included or kept back.
overview: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that a grafted carob and a sycamore trunk are not sold along with a field. רב יהודה in the name of רב brings it from the sale of שדה עפרון to אברהם: only trees that are 'within the borders all around' are included. רב משרשיא learns from the same פסוק that borders are part of a sale מן התורה. Then רב יהודה advises that a land sale document should list the palm trees and smaller growths, even though the buyer gets them anyway. The גמרא goes through several ways a seller might describe the sale ('land and palms', 'land with palms', 'land of palms', 'except for this palm') and what each wording means. Next it rules on what a seller keeps when he sells a field 'except for the trees', depending on which kinds of trees, palms or vines are in the field. Finally רב gives a rope test: only a tree big enough that you must climb it with a rope counts as kept by the seller.

steps.title: What is the source for the exclusion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that a grafted carob and a sycamore trunk are not sold together with a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that certain big trees are not included when a field is sold. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a grafted carob and a sycamore trunk stay with the seller even when he sells the field. The גמרא wants to know what this is based on, since most trees are sold with the field.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)
A grafted carob tree (from the משנה)
The trunk of a sycamore tree (from the משנה)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's rule that a grafted carob and a sycamore trunk are not sold with the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by asking for the source of the משנה's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A Torah source for why a grafted carob and a sycamore trunk are not included in a field sale.

steps.title: The source is the field of עפרון
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב learns from the sale of שדה עפרון that only trees which need the field's border around them are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the פסוק says 'And the field of Ephron in Machpelah was established...' This means trees that need a border around them are included. These trees, which do not need a border around them, are left out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question with the פסוק about אברהם buying the field of עפרון. The פסוק says the trees 'within all its borders around' were sold, so only trees that depend on the field's border are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary small trees are 'part of the field' and are marked off only by the field's border. A grafted carob or a sycamore trunk is so big and important that it stands out on its own, like a separate item. So it is not counted as one of the trees 'inside the border' and is not sold with the field.

keyTerms.meaning: As the פסוק says
The field of עפרון that אברהם bought
A border all around
These are excluded

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the rule for which trees go with a field in a sale: trees that are part of the field go, trees that stand as their own item do not.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
As the verse states:
"So the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 23:17. The 'etc.' points to the end of the פסוק: 'all the trees in the field, within all its borders around.'

phrases.english: Something that needs a border around it is included.
These are excluded,
since they do not need a border around them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about שדה עפרון includes only trees 'within the borders around'; trees that stand out on their own are excluded.

steps.title: Borders are part of a sale from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא learns from the same פסוק that the borders of a field are acquired in a sale on a Torah level.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said: from here we learn that borders are from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא adds another lesson from the same פסוק. Since the פסוק mentions the borders, we learn that the borders of a field are part of a sale on a Torah level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself lists the borders as part of what אברהם got. So the borders of a field are not just a later custom; they are included in the sale by the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: From here
Borders (of a field)
From the Torah, on a Torah level

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of שדה עפרון teaches two things: big separate trees are not sold with a field, and borders are part of a sale מן התורה.

phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said:
From here we have a source that borders are from the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an extra lesson from the same פסוק quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The borders of a field are acquired in a sale on a Torah level, based on the פסוק of שדה עפרון.

steps.title: Spelling out the trees in a sale document
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה advises that a seller of land should list the palm trees and their parts in the document, even though the buyer gets them anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: someone who sells land to his friend should write for him: 'Acquire for yourself the palm trees, young palms, branches and shoots.' Even though the buyer acquires them even if this is not written, it is still a nice improvement of the document.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives practical advice: when you sell land, write out the trees and growths in the document. This is not required by law, it just makes the document better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By law the buyer already gets these trees, since they are part of the field. Writing them out clearly prevents any future argument between buyer and seller. This is called a 'beauty of the document', meaning a good extra, not a must.

keyTerms.meaning: Who sells land
Palm trees
Young palms, branches, and shoots (smaller growths in the field)
An improvement of the document; a good extra, not a requirement

steps.confusionAlert: צריך למכתב here does not mean the sale fails without it. The גמרא says right away that the buyer acquires these anyway; writing them is only to make the document clearer.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
One who sells land to his friend
should write for him:
"Acquire for yourself the palm trees and the young palms
and the branches and the shoots."

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי לָא כְּתַב לֵיהּ הָכִי – קְנֵי,
phrases.english: And even though if he did not write this for him, he still acquires them,
even so, it is an improvement of the document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: הַאי מַאן דִּמְזַבֵּן אַרְעָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new practical topic about how to write a land sale document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller should list the palm trees and smaller growths in the document; the buyer gets them even without it, but writing it is better.

steps.title: Selling 'land and palm trees'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller sold 'land and palm trees', he must give two palm trees, buying or redeeming them if needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to him 'land and palm trees', we check: if he has palm trees, he gives him two palm trees. If he has none, he must buy him two palm trees. If his palm trees are mortgaged, he must redeem two palm trees for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at different ways a seller can describe a sale. Here he said 'land AND palm trees', so the palm trees are a separate promise he must keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' makes the palm trees a second item being sold, not a description of the land. So the seller owes at least two trees, the smallest number called 'trees'. If he has none, or they are mortgaged, he must still get two for the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: We look and check the situation
Two palm trees (the smallest number for 'trees')
They are mortgaged, pledged to someone else
He redeems, buys back from a lender

phrases.english: If he said to him: "Land and palm trees," we look:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לֵיהּ דִּיקְלֵי – יָהֵיב לֵיהּ תְּרֵי דִיקְלֵי,
phrases.english: if he has palm trees, he gives him two palm trees;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לֵית לֵיהּ – זָבֵין לֵיהּ תְּרֵי דִיקְלֵי,
phrases.english: and if he does not have any, he buys him two palm trees;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי מְשַׁעְבְּדִי – פָּרֵיק לֵיהּ תְּרֵי דִיקְלֵי.
phrases.english: and if they are mortgaged, he redeems two palm trees for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of sale documents by looking at the exact wording used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Land and palm trees' obligates the seller to provide two palm trees, buying or redeeming them if needed.

steps.title: Selling 'land with palm trees'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller sold 'land with palm trees' and there are no palms on it, the sale is a mistaken sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'land with palm trees', we check: if there are palm trees on it, he gives it to him. If not, it is a mistaken sale.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the seller said 'land WITH palm trees'. This describes the land itself, so we check if the land really has palm trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the palm trees are not a separate promise; they describe what kind of land is being sold. If the land has no palm trees, the description was false. So the whole sale is cancelled as a mistaken sale, and the seller does not have to go buy trees.

keyTerms.meaning: With palm trees (describing the land)
A mistaken sale, which is cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: Compare with step 5: 'and palm trees' means the seller must supply trees, but 'with palm trees' means that if there are none, the sale itself is cancelled.

phrases.english: If he said "Land with palm trees," we look:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית בַּהּ דִּיקְלֵי – יָהֵיב לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: if there are palm trees on it, he gives it to him;
and if not, it is a mistaken sale.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second wording, contrasted with 'land and palm trees'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Land with palm trees' describes the land; if there are no palms, the sale is a מקח טעות.

steps.title: Selling 'land of palm trees'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller sold 'land of palm trees', the buyer cannot demand palms, because it means land good for growing palms.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'land of palm trees', the buyer has no claim to palm trees, because he only told him the land is fit for palm trees.
steps.whatsHappening: The seller said 'a land of palm trees'. The גמרא explains this only describes the type of soil, not trees that are there now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Land of palm trees' means land suited for growing palms. So the buyer has no claim for trees, and the sale is not a mistaken sale even if no palms stand there.

keyTerms.meaning: A place of palm trees; land suited for palms
That is fit, suitable

phrases.english: If he said "Land of palm trees," the buyer has no claim to palm trees,
because he was telling him that it is fit for palm trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third wording, contrasted with 'with palm trees'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Land of palm trees' only means land fit for palms; the buyer has no claim to trees and the sale stands.

steps.title: Selling land 'except for a certain palm tree'
steps.stepSummary: If the seller excludes one palm tree, it depends on its quality: a good tree means only it is kept; a bad tree means the better ones are kept too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'except for such-and-such a palm tree', we check: if it is a good palm tree, he kept only that one. If it is a bad palm tree, then all the more so he kept the other ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The seller sold the land but said 'except for this palm tree'. The גמרא checks the quality of that tree to understand what he meant to keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he held back a good tree, it makes sense he only wanted that one, so the rest go to the buyer. If he held back a bad tree, he surely did not mean to give away the better ones, so he kept those too.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for
So-and-so, a certain one
He held it back for himself
All the more so

steps.whatToRemember: The exact wording of a sale decides what is included: 'and palms' = must supply two; 'with palms' = sale void if none; 'of palms' = only fit for palms; 'except this palm' = depends if that tree is good or bad.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְבַר מִדִּיקְלָא פְּלָנְיָא – חָזֵינַן;
phrases.english: If he said to him: "Except for such-and-such a palm tree," we look:

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּיקְלָא טָבָא הוּא – שַׁיּוֹרֵי שַׁיְּירֵיהּ,
phrases.english: if it is a good palm tree, he held back only that one;

phrases.aramaic: אִי דִּיקְלָא בִּישָׁא הוּא – כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן הָנָךְ.
phrases.english: if it is a bad palm tree, all the more so he held back those others.
phrases.notes: 'Those others' are the better palm trees in the field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְבַר מִדִּיקְלָא פְּלָנְיָא – חָזֵינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth wording case, about holding one tree back from the sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Excluding a good tree keeps only that tree; excluding a bad tree means the better trees are also kept by the seller.

steps.title: Selling a field except for the trees when there is only one kind
steps.stepSummary: If the seller sells the field "except for the trees," he keeps whatever single type of tree-like plant is in the field: regular trees, palms, or vines.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the seller says "except for the trees": if the field has regular trees, he keeps the trees. If it has only palm trees, he keeps the palm trees. If it has only vines, he keeps the vines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new case. The seller excludes "the trees" from the sale, and we decide what he keeps when the field has only one kind of plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the word אילני means regular trees, not palms or vines. But if the field has no regular trees, the seller must have meant something real, so we apply his words to whatever is actually there.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for. This is the seller's words for keeping something out of the sale.
Trees. This means regular trees, like olive or fig trees.
Palm trees
Grapevines
If he has. The field contains this.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think palms and vines are always called "trees." They count here only because the field has no regular trees for the seller's words to apply to.

phrases.english: If he said to him: "except for the trees"
phrases.notes: The seller is telling the buyer he sells the whole field, but not the trees.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לֵיהּ אִילָנֵי, לְבַר מֵאִילָנֵי.
phrases.english: If he has trees, it is except for the trees.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לֵיהּ דִּיקְלֵי – לְבַר מִדִּיקְלֵי.
phrases.english: If he has palm trees, it is except for the palm trees.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אִית לֵיהּ גּוּפְנֵי – לְבַר מִגּוּפְנֵי.
phrases.english: If he has grapevines, it is except for the grapevines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rules about what a seller keeps when he excludes trees. Step 8 was about excluding one palm; now he excludes "the trees" in general.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "Except for the trees" covers whatever single kind of tree, palm, or vine is in the field.

steps.title: Which kind is kept when the field has two kinds
steps.stepSummary: When the field has two types, the גמרא rules which one "trees" refers to: regular trees beat vines and palms, and vines beat palms.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are trees and vines, he keeps the trees. If there are trees and palms, he keeps the trees. If there are vines and palms, he keeps the vines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now handles a field with two kinds of plants and decides which kind the word "trees" refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When regular trees are there, the word אילני means them, so the vines or palms are sold with the field. When there are only vines and palms, the גמרא rules that the vines are kept and the palms go to the buyer. The גמרא gives no reason for ranking vines above palms; it simply states the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Trees and vines. Both kinds are in the field.
Trees and palms
Vines and palms

steps.whatToRemember: "Except for the trees" keeps regular trees first. If there are none, it keeps vines before palms. Whatever is not kept goes to the buyer.

phrases.english: Trees and vines: it is except for the trees.
phrases.notes: So the vines are sold to the buyer along with the field.

phrases.english: Trees and palms: it is except for the trees.
Vines and palms: it is except for the vines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 9 from a field with one kind of plant to a field with two kinds.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Order of priority for "trees": regular trees, then vines, then palms. Only the top kind present is kept.

steps.title: רב's rope test for which trees the seller keeps
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a tree you must climb with a rope is kept by the seller, and a tree you don't need a rope for is sold with the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Any tree you climb with a rope counts as kept by the seller. Any tree you do not climb with a rope does not count as kept.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a practical size test for which trees the seller keeps when he sells a field without its trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is a measurement. Only a tree big enough that you need a rope to climb it counts as a real tree that the seller kept. Smaller trees go to the buyer with the field.

keyTerms.meaning: Climb it. People go up the tree, for example to pick its fruit.
Rope
Something held back. The part the seller keeps out of the sale.
It is, or it counts as.

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns the general wording rules into a clear test that tells you which trees stay with the seller.

phrases.english: Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁעוֹלִין לוֹ בְּחֶבֶל – הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר,
phrases.english: Any tree that one climbs by rope counts as kept back,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין עוֹלִין לוֹ בְּחֶבֶל – לָא הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר.
phrases.english: any tree that one does not climb by rope does not count as kept back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כֹּל שֶׁעוֹלִין לוֹ בְּחֶבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a size test to the rule about keeping trees out of a sale.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trees that need a rope to climb are kept by the seller. Smaller trees go to the buyer.
